To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plane of nutrition (PN; i.e. the level of feed offered) offered to ewes during their first winter and pregnancy affected the performance of their progeny, but that PN offered during the summer had little effect.

(1) increasing plane of nutrition offered to ewe lambs during mid and late-pregnancy had a significant effect on ewe BW, lamb birth weight, lamb survival and weaning weight and (2) increasing plane of nutrient during the rearing period (8 to 18 months of age) had no effect on ewe reproductive performance or on lamb performance.

increasing PN offered to ewe replacement during mid and late gestation (i.e. winter_2) increased ewe BW, lamb birth and weaning BW, reduced the proportion of non-pregnant ewes and had no effect on litter size, number of lambs weaned or lamb performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system of ewe replacement rearing that optimises reproductive efficiency of the ewe and growth performance of her lambs.
the effects of nutrition on the performance of replacement ewes during the rearing and first pregnancy phases and on their progeny during their first year of life.
the effects of PN during the rearing and pregnancy phases on ewe and lamb performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increasing PN during mid to late pregnancy has the greatest effect on reproductive performance of the ewe and growth of the progeny.
PN offered to replacement ewes during mid and late gestation had a greater effect on performance of the ewe and her progeny than did PN offered during winter of the rearing phase.
increasing PN offered during mid and late-pregnancy had the greatest effect of the PN treatments examined on ewe and lamb performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for ewe lambs, the most important period of the rearing phase is mid and late pregnancy.

PN offered during the rearing of replacement ewes and during mid and late gestation has a significant effect on ewe, lamb and progeny performance, but that there is no interaction between PN and ewes' genotype.
, among the genotypes studied, Bel×SBF and BelMG×SBFs were the most productive genotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PN offered to ewe lambs during their first pregnancy has a major impact on their subsequent reproductive performance and that of their progeny.
the PN during mid and, in particular, late pregnancy had the most impact on ewe and lamb performance.
the nutritional status of ewe replacements during mid and late gestation has a significant influence on their reproductive and progeny performances.
